newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Deja vu for Sharks and Blues - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Deja vu for Sharks and Blues - Clarke.

text.p: AUCKLAND, May 23 - Auckland Blues centre Eroni Clarke is experiencing a sense of deja vu ahead of Saturday's Super 12 rugby semifinal against the Natal Sharks at Eden Park, NZPA reports.
Clarke says both teams have been down this road before, experienced the adrenalin and know what is at stake compared to Wellington Hurricanes and ACT Brumbies on the other side of the draw.
"There is always a fear factor when you get to this stage," Clarke said.
"Natal haven't come here to lose and we aren't prepared to lose. We have prepared ourselves to win -- but it is always at the back of your mind.
"But if everyone prepares well then you know all you can do is go out and do the best you can."
Named in the All Black trials this week after being out in the wilderness in recent years, Clarke said the intensity at training this week has been special.
"This is semifinal, final time. Natal and we know all about that. We've been down this road before so we know what it is like," Clarke said.
"I don't think ACT and Wellington really know what it is like, it is a whole new experience for them.
"The enthusiasm will be there because we've been here before so it will be a hard-fought, tough, typical battle."
Clarke said the Sharks with Jeremy Thomson and Pieter Muller in the centres will prove a tough nut to crack and with the return of Andre Joubert at fullback they have become an even more potent side.
"They have a strong powerful backline with good defence," he said.
"With Muller and Thomson in the midfield it is not an easy backline to play and now with Andre (Joubert) coming back anything can happen.
"I do rate their backline. It is right at the top and probably the best backline in South Africa.
"That is why they are in the semifinals. That is why they are here."
Joubert, in particular, poses a threat that even surpasses that of All Blacks fullback Christian Cullen, Clarke said.
"The thing that Joubert brings in is experience, he's been around a long, long time and accumulated a wealth of experience," he said.
"That is why he is such a danger."
Clarke said Auckland are aware they will have to show a marked improvement on anything they have done this year.
"It isn't just about lifting it up a notch, this is it, this is crunchtime, this is semifinal time," he said.
"It is the do-or-die situation and both teams have prepared for it, so we know what to expect."
For the Sharks, coach Ian McIntosh is demanding they return to doing things that worked for them before going off the rails in recent matches.
"We need to get our game back, we've been a bit off-track a little because we've got some players missing," he said.
"We have to go back to what we know and how we play best.
"We obviously have a few variations that we intend to put into place during the game and we've been working on that.
"We have our thoughts on where we have to shut them down and it is a question we have to answer on Saturday.
"The biggest thing about Auckland is that they have been playing awesome rugby, they're a very balanced side and they have hard and fast runners with skill."
Both teams wrapped up their preparations yesterday.
Teams:-

Auckland Blues: Adrian Cashmore, Joeli Vidiri, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Ofisa Tonu'u, Zinzan Brooke (captain), Mark Carter, Robin Brooke, Leo Lafaiali'i, Michael Jones, Olo Brown, Sean Fitzpatrick, Craig Dowd.

Natal Sharks: Andre Joubert, Joos Joubert, Jeremy Thomson, Shaun Payne, Pieter Muller, Henry Honiball, Kevin Putt, Gary Teichmann (captain), Wayne Fyvie, Wayne Boardman, John Slade, Wickus van Heerden, Adrian Garvey, John Allan, Rob Kempson.
